newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia Rosgosstrakh happy with privatisation.
newsitem.headline: Russia Rosgosstrakh happy with privatisation.

text.p: The chairman of Russia's biggest insurer Rosgosstrakh said on Wednesday he was happy about the privatisation scheme for his company and said it would not be sold off cheap.
A government spokesman said on Tuesday that the government was worried by a low valuation of 2.13 billion roubles of the company set for the company for its forthcoming privatisation.
But Rosgosstrakh Chairman Vladislav Reznik told Reuters the figure referred to the company's authorised capital.
"I would be distressed myself, if Rosgosstrakh was sold at this price, but it will not be so," he said.
He said Rosgosstrakh was being privatised and its employees had already subscribed for 20 percent of its shares.
The price of the shares will be defined by the Russian Federal Property Fund soon, he said.

According to the scheme of privatisation chosen by Rosgosstrakh employees, they will have a priority right to buy a further 30 percent of shares, while the remaining 50 percent will go to a cash auction, Reznik said.
"It is a legal scheme and it suits us, as it gives the working collective privileges," he said.
